title: Electric Duotone — Wired-Loud Feature Opener
description: A Wired-era editorial opener where a geometric display-sans headline crashes over a cyan-magenta duotone hero, balanced by an italic serif subhead and a bold section-tag chip — the opinionated Scott Dadich grid, translated to slides.
philosophy: This template exists to make the image and the headline fight, not coexist. Borrowed directly from the Scott Dadich Wired playbook, it rejects the safe margin and drives type into photography to manufacture instant visual tension — a section chip announces the story's territory before the eye even settles. It is for speakers who want an audience to feel a tech-culture story before they read a word, in rooms where projector contrast makes duotone sizzle. What it refuses: tasteful whitespace, neutral grids, and any layout that whispers when it should shout.
goodFor: Tech-culture keynote and conference feature openers
Bold editorial brand retrospectives and campaign launches
Speaker-as-author contexts where strong point of view is the whole point
avoidFor: Pastel wellness or consumer lifestyle brands
Decks requiring full-color photography anywhere on the hero slide
author: harness

examples.promptCore: Confrontational editorial energy from the Wired feature-opener tradition — the slide should feel like a magazine spread, not a deck slide. A full-bleed duotone hero is processed into two clashing hues that feel electric, not photographic. The headline drives into the image like graffiti on architecture — asymmetric and aggressive — while a section-chip claims territory at the entry corner and the italic serif subhead provides the only moment of restraint.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed duotone hero occupies the entire canvas with zero safe-margin buffer. 12-column grid; the display headline lands in cols 1–10, baseline anchored at approximately two-thirds down the slide, deliberately overlapping the photo subject to manufacture collision. A section-tag chip anchors top-left at the outer grid edge as a story-territory marker. The italic serif subhead drops immediately below the headline within cols 1–8, separated from it by a thin rule line.

examples.promptCore: Wired feature-well energy: a dominant stat or pull-quote fragment functions as a second headline, anchored by a tight italic attribution below it. The composition feels like a magazine spread mid-story — asymmetric tension between a dense left column and a sparse right rail cleaved by a hard vertical rule. Mood is authoritative and kinetic, like a feature writer mid-argument, the layout leaning forward rather than sitting still. Avoid centered arrangements, decorative dividers, or any airy softness that would bleed the editorial tension dry.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; primary content occupies cols 1–8 with a narrow left bleed that lets type press against the slide edge, while cols 10–12 form a sparse right rail reserved for a section chip or single callout element. A vertical rule at col 9 serves as the hard structural spine dividing the two zones. Hierarchy is driven by extreme size contrast — one oversized pull-quote fragment or stat dominates the left column, with tight attribution or supporting copy sitting below at dramatically reduced scale. Page number anchors bottom-right; no top header band, section identity is carried solely by the chip.
